requests.why:
You asked me to price this up. I have read all 23 pages of the ITT, the estate plan, the SMA profile and all six images, and the honest answer is that nobody can price it yet.

1. THERE ARE NO DIMENSIONS. No door schedule, no size, no elevation, no opening register, no drawing. The 'Block Plan' is an estate plan of parking spaces and flat stacks. The only visual information is five photographs. A fabricator cannot quote five doorsets without five sizes, so no RFQ can go out and there is no price. Jordan Jones has offered to meet us on site - that offer is the answer. And the pack shuts the door on fixing it later: 1.4.2 and 3.1.2 both say no claim for extras will be entertained for anything a site visit would have revealed, and 3.1.1 deems us to have visited.

2. SIGNING THEIR FORM OF TENDER DELETES OUR EXCLUSIONS. Section 5.0 clause 4.1: 'any caveats, assumptions, reservations or exclusions that may be printed on correspondence emanating from the tender ... shall not be applicable'. The clause above it offers the works 'For the firm price contained within the pricing summary'. Signing that page is how you submit - there is no unsigned route. So our whole standard exclusions schedule is disapplied here: access plant, waste removal, making good, access control. On this job an item is either priced or accepted in writing before 9am on the 24th. There is no third option. I have added a check rule for it so it fires on the next tender that does this.

3. THE INTERCOM CANNOT WORK ON THE HARDWARE THEY HAVE SPECIFIED. They require the intercom proven working on completion; their own hardware list is a mechanical cylinder with a thumbturn and nothing else - no electric strike, no keep, no rectifier, no power transfer. The entry panels are on the brickwork beside each door in all five photos, so they are not moving; the work is inside the new doorset and it is a door-entry specialist's. Clause 2.1.4 wants every subcontractor named WITH the tender, so we need one chosen before we submit, not after.

4. TWO PASS/FAIL GATES I CANNOT CHECK. Clause 4.3.2 sets PL insurance at a minimum of GBP 10,000,000, and 2.5 requires a Waste Carrier Licence enclosed with the tender. Neither is recorded anywhere I can see. If we fall short on either, the survey day is wasted and I would rather know now.

WHAT IT IS WORTH. Benchmark only, supplier-anchored, size assumed: GBP 24k-26k for the five doorsets - frames, glass and fit - from Bellview's own Smart Wall Pocket quotes (Lyttleton 0000000445 pos 011 at GBP 2,930.12 net for a 1600x2100 door + fixed field is the closest match we have). Sensitivity across plausible sizes and rates is GBP 21,700-29,600. That is probably about half the tender: strip-out AND disposal, making good inside and out, the intercom work, 129 keys, the client's own Preliminaries line and their own Contingency line are all extra and not one of them has a rate in our register - 0 of 80 categories. Our pricing document answers one of the three lines on their pricing summary, which is exactly what prompted Guildmore's question about removal.

ONE THING WORTH TELLING THEM EITHER WAY. Their ITT names the blocks 1-6, 7-16, 17-23, 24-31, 32-39. Their own estate plan and the nameplates in their own photographs both say 1-6, 7-15, 16-23, 24-31, 32-39, with no flat 13 on the estate - and their key count settles it: 38 flats x 3 + 5 doorsets x 3 = 129, exactly the figure they ask for, where 39 flats would give 132. Flat 16 is served by the third door, not the second. It matters because the keys are five differs, so anyone cutting them off their block ranges orders 33 and 24 where 27 and 27 are needed.

Timeline is tighter than 27 days looks: survey, then RFQ, then about a week for Bellview, then price, check and issue, against a 9am Monday deadline. The survey wants to happen in the first week of August. Full write-up in data/jobs/john-north-hall.md; checks manifest is at 3 FAIL, 2 ASK and nothing has been issued.
